short: Mathematician and physicist who unified terrestrial and celestial motion.
full:
Isaac Newton's Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687) set out three laws of motion and a law of universal gravitation, and demonstrated that the same rules govern a falling apple and an orbiting moon. It is arguably the single most consequential scientific book ever published.

He also invented the calculus independently of Leibniz, decomposed white light into the spectrum, and built the first practical reflecting telescope. He spent at least as much effort on alchemy and biblical chronology, which he did not regard as separate pursuits. In later life he ran the Royal Mint, reformed the coinage and prosecuted counterfeiters with considerable enthusiasm.
